title: K Closest Points to Origin
prompt: You are given an array of 2D points, where each point is a pair [x, y], and an integer k. Return the k points that are closest to the origin (0,0), measured by Euclidean distance. The returned points may be in any order. Duplicate points at the same coordinates are allowed. If k equals the total number of points, return all of them.

title: Matrix Block Sum
prompt: You are given an m x n matrix of integers, mat, and an integer k. Return a matrix ans of the same size where ans[i][j] is the sum of all elements mat[r][c] inside the square block centered at (i,j) with half-width k, clamped to the matrix borders. Cells that fall outside the matrix are ignored. When k is 0, each block is just the single cell itself.

title: Top K Frequent Elements
prompt: You are given an array of integers, nums, and an integer k. Return the k most frequently occurring values in the array, in any order. When several values tie in frequency, any choice among them is acceptable. The result must contain exactly k distinct values, and k is between 1 and the number of distinct values in nums.

title: Rotate Image
prompt: You are given an n x n matrix of integers representing an image. Rotate the image 90 degrees clockwise and return the rotated matrix. The rotation must be done in place, meaning you may modify the input matrix directly and use only O(1) extra memory. A 1x1 matrix is unchanged, and rotating the matrix twice produces a 180-degree rotation.

title: Find Median from Data Stream
prompt: Design a data structure that receives a stream of integers one at a time. Add each new number with addNum(num), and find the median of all numbers added so far with findMedian(). When the count of added numbers is odd, the median is the middle element; when it is even, the median is the average of the two middle elements, returned as a float. Each operation must run in O(log n) time.

title: Trie Prefix Match - Case #6
prompt: You are given a list of words and a prefix string. Build a Trie (Prefix Tree) data structure that stores every word so prefix queries can be answered quickly. Return all words that begin with the given prefix, including the word itself if it is stored in the trie. If no word matches the prefix, return an empty list. Each word should appear at most once in the result, even if it was inserted more than once. The solution should handle short words, a prefix that matches every word, and a prefix that matches nothing.

title: Two Pointer Container - Case #7
prompt: You are given an array of non-negative integers, height, where each value is the height of a vertical line drawn at that index. Two lines, together with the x-axis, form a container. The amount of water a pair of lines can hold is min(height[i], height[j]) multiplied by the distance between them, (j - i). Return the maximum water area any pair of lines can hold as a single integer. If the array has fewer than two lines, the answer is 0. Heights can be zero and may repeat.

title: Monotonic Stack Evaluation - Case #8
prompt: You are given an array of integers, nums. For each element, find the next element to its right that is strictly greater than it and put that value in the same position of the result array. If no such element exists, use -1. The result array has the same length as nums. The array may contain duplicates, negative numbers, and zeros. A monotonic stack lets each element be pushed and popped at most once, so the whole solution runs in O(n) time.

title: Tree Level Order Traversal - Case #9
prompt: You are given the root of a binary tree. Return the level-order traversal of the tree as a list of lists, where the first inner list holds the root value and each following inner list holds the values of all nodes at one deeper depth, ordered from left to right. An empty tree returns an empty list, and a tree with a single node returns [[rootValue]]. Use a queue to visit nodes level by level, ignoring missing children so each level list contains only real values.

title: Array Prefix Sum - Case #10

title: Binary Search Range - Case #11

title: Dynamic Programming State - Case #12

Return a two-element array [first, last] where first is the index of the first occurrence of target and last is the index of the last occurrence. title: Dynamic Programming State - Case #472
prompt: You are given an m x n grid of integers where each cell grid[r][c] holds a cost. Return the minimum total cost of a valid path, where the path cost is the sum of the values in every visited cell, including both the start and end cells. A 1x1 grid returns the value of its only cell.

title: Graph Topological Sort - Case #473

title: Sliding Window Maximum - Case #474

title: Trie Prefix Match - Case #476

title: Monotonic Stack Evaluation - Case #478
